results.question: Do you ship to Spain?
results.answer: Yes, we ship to Spain. Larchwick now delivers to every country in the European Union [1][3]. Shipping within the EU is a flat €5, and free on orders over €40 [2].

results.question: How much does shipping cost?
results.answer: Shipping is a flat €5 within the EU, and it's free on orders over €40 [1]. We ship to every country in the European Union [2].

results.question: How soon will my coffee arrive after I order?
results.answer: Most orders arrive in 3–6 working days, and they leave our roastery within 48 hours of roasting, since we roast on Mondays and Thursdays [2][1]. You can check the roast date on every bag, and coffee tastes best from about 5 to 30 days after roasting [1].

results.question: Which days do you roast?
results.answer: We roast to order on Mondays and Thursdays, so nothing sits on a shelf for weeks [3]. You can find more about our process on [our about page](/about/).

results.question: Can I buy ground coffee for a French press?
results.answer: Yes, we sell ground coffee, and you can choose a grind for French press [1]. For French press, the grind should be coarse, about the size of sea salt [5]. You can find more on our [products page](/products/).

results.question: How should I store my beans?
results.answer: Store your beans in their original bag, which has a one-way valve, or in an airtight container, away from light, heat and moisture. Please don't keep them in the fridge [1]. Whole beans also stay fresh longer than ground coffee [3].

results.question: Is your coffee organic?
results.answer: Some of our coffees are grown without chemicals, but not all farms can afford organic certification, so we don't label our coffee as organic [1]. For more detail, see our [FAQ](/faq/).

results.question: How does the subscription work and can I pause it?
results.answer: Our subscription lets you choose a coffee, a size and a delivery frequency of every 2 or 4 weeks, and you save 10% on every delivery [3]. You can pause or cancel any time, with no minimum period [1][4].

results.question: What does the Colombia Huila taste like?
results.answer: Our Colombia Huila tastes of caramel, red apple and cocoa [2]. With milk, the chocolate side becomes stronger, which makes it a good match for a flat white or cappuccino [1].

results.question: Which coffee is best for pour-over?
results.answer: For pour-over drinkers who take their coffee black, our site recommends the Ethiopia Yirgacheffe [5]. If you want something sweet and easy, the Colombia Huila is another option [5]. You can find more on choosing the right grind for your brew in our [pour-over guide](/blog/how-to-brew-pour-over-at-home/) [2].

results.question: How much is a 1 kg bag of House Espresso?
results.answer: A 1 kg bag of House Espresso costs €40 [1]. Our 250 g bag is €12 [3], and you can see all sizes and prices on our [products page](/products/).

results.question: Until when is the Autumn Blend available?
results.answer: The Autumn Blend is available until the end of November [2][3]. We roast it in small batches every week during that time, and once it sells out, it returns next year [2].

results.question: Do you supply cafés with wholesale coffee?
results.answer: Yes, we supply cafés with fresh-roasted espresso and filter coffee, with weekly or twice-weekly delivery and no minimum contract [4]. Wholesale espresso starts from €24/kg with a 5 kg minimum per delivery [5]. You can [contact us](/contact/) for free taste samples.

results.question: How many people fit in a brewing class?
results.answer: Our brewing classes are small-group sessions with a maximum of six people, and all equipment is provided [1][2]. You can find more on our [services page](/services/).

results.question: What grind size do I need for cold brew?
results.answer: For cold brew, use an extra coarse grind, similar to cracked pepper [1][2]. Our cold brew recipe calls for 100 g of coffee to 800 g of cold, filtered water, steeped 12–18 hours [2].

results.question: Why is my French press coffee bitter?
results.answer: Bitterness in French press is often caused by a grind that's too fine, since fine particles pass through the mesh and over-extract, so try a coarse grind about the size of sea salt [1]. Leaving coffee sitting in the press after brewing can also keep extracting and add bitterness, so pour it out right after pressing [3]. You can read more in our [French press mistakes guide](/blog/french-press-5-common-mistakes/) or our [grind size guide](/blog/choosing-the-right-grind-size/) [2][5].

results.question: What is the difference between washed and natural coffee?
results.answer: Washed coffee has the fruit removed right after picking, then the beans are fermented briefly, washed clean and dried, giving a clean, bright taste with clear acidity [1]. Natural coffee dries the whole cherry in the sun for several weeks before the dried fruit is removed, which gives a fruitier, sweeter cup with a heavier body [2]. You can read more on our [washed vs natural process guide](/blog/washed-vs-natural-process/).

results.question: Who roasts the coffee at Larchwick?
results.answer: Mira Holt is Larchwick's head roaster, and she joined after eight years as a barista and trainer [1]. Larchwick was founded by Tomas Varga, who still does the cupping every Friday [5].
